title: Okta is up on a sector bounce, not its own headline. Does that kind ofmove hold after Palo Alto reports tonight?
author: tickeron_community
selftext:
\[OKTA\]([https://tickeron.com/ticker/OKTA/](https://tickeron.com/ticker/OKTA/)) jumped 6.90% in the midday  
write-up, from the prior close of $174.54 to $186.58, entirely during  
regular hours. Later prints were stronger, around +11.6%, so the  
midday figure is already stale.  
  
The gain came from a sector-wide rebound in cybersecurity software  
after a month-long rout. Morgan Stanley turned more constructive on  
security names, citing healthy demand checks and a sector multiple  
back near its one-year average, and kept Okta among its preferred  
identity-security picks. No Okta-specific earnings print drove this.  
\[PANW\]([https://tickeron.com/ticker/PANW/](https://tickeron.com/ticker/PANW/)) reports after the close.  
  
The write-up on why \[OKTA\]([https://tickeron.com/ticker/OKTA/](https://tickeron.com/ticker/OKTA/)) bounced  
with the cyber group today:  
[https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-okta-inc-okta-stock-up-6-89-today-40588/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-okta-inc-okta-stock-up-6-89-today-40588/)  
  
If the only real catalyst is a sector call and a looming  
\[PANW\]([https://tickeron.com/ticker/PANW/](https://tickeron.com/ticker/PANW/)) print, is this bounce  
durable?  
  
Not financial advice. Figures are from today's midday write-up, not a  
live quote, and the gain has already widened.
